newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable despite ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable despite ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Monday despite excess rupiah supply, dealers said.
They said trading was slow, with overall focus seen on Tuesday's liquidity condition due to a large amount of tax payments due at the end of the 1996/97 fiscal year on March 31.
"Liquidity is ample but operators keep pouring dollars into the market. This seems to renew speculation of another band widening," one European bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,403.75/04.20 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,404.75/05.75.

Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,404.25/04.50 and 2,404.25/04.60 respectively. Some dealers said speculation of a band widening might have resulted from option trades on the rupiah which bet on a dollar-rupiah band widening.
They said the relative pressure on the dollar could also be coming from operators' fear over a possible sudden tightening in the money market as tax payments were expected to be large.
However, short-term money suggested a calm market, with overnight money traded at 1.0/2.0 percent in the afternoon.
Dealers said liquidity was the main issue although players were looking for a possible rate hike in the United States.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will hold a meeting on Tuesday to consider raising interest rates.
The European bank dealer said the U.S. decision will certainly have implications on the attractiveness of the rupiah but, at present, local focus was on the fiscal-year end.
He said many operators were seen covering short positions in the swap market which they had established earlier.
"Operators are uncertain over the liquidity condition after the fiscal end. The new reserve rate will also soon become effective. They tend to cash out at present," the dealer said.
He said operators would establish fresh short positions if liquidity remained ample after the month-end and fiscal-year end.
Dealers said the increase of the reserve requirement rate from three to five percent from April 16 was quite significant, keeping operators cautious on the liquidity outlook.
One-month swaps were at 9.0/10.0, two at 20.5/21.5, three at 31.0/32.5 and six at 68.00/68.75 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band on Monday at 2,391/2,583 and the conversion band at 2,391/2,439.
